body:
**The first full year of the converted position, and it is fluent.** 2021 has
only 34 posts, but the vocabulary, the targets and the internal disagreements
are all a settled leftist's rather than a recent convert's — and one of them
corrects a date this corpus currently carries.

## The position, a year on

The 2020 declaration was an ultimatum. 2021 is the working version:

- **5 January**, on GOP rhetoric: *"just wait until they are running against a principled and unapologetic dem soc... they will probz regret using up all their effective 'socialism bad because venezuala' talking points"*
- **6 January**, refusing an anti-Comey op-ed's framing: *"Comey is not 'what got us into this mess'. The Democratic party and their corporate ring-kissing deserve blame; also - racism."*
- **6 November**, on the infrastructure bill: *"None of the remaining entitlements will substantially improve material conditions and nothing will be implemented before the midterm election anyway"*
- **3–4 December**, on the Fetterman/Lamb primary: *"the neoliberal forces who run the party and their corpo donors see it as a worthy investment to block fetterman"*, and *"I hope that his potential for the left isn't the catalyst for the same playbook that worked to outperform both Sanders campaigns"*
- **15 November**: *"Honestly I would sooner forgive someone for viciously insulting my mom than I would for taking a swipe at Bernie Sanders."*

*Material conditions*, *neoliberal*, *corpo donors*, *dem soc* — the terms are
used correctly and the primary opponent is the Democratic Party rather than the
Republicans, which is the tell that distinguishes a leftist from a liberal.
`@hasanthehun` — Hasan Piker, one of the four channels
`wiki/mind/synthesis/2020-left-turn` names as the pipeline — is addressed
directly on 9 January.

And on **15 November**, a disappointment stated as one: *"Had been (foolishly)
holding out hope that @elonmusk would eventually turn face and experience some
kind of leftist epiphany. Officially filing that fantasy as a 'no shot' and
also get fucked, Elon."* The admission that he had been hoping is the
interesting half.

## 26 October 2021 corrects a date

`wiki/interests/opie-and-anthony` dates Dan's move away from comedy free-speech
absolutism to **28 March 2022**, during the Chris Rock slap. This page has it
five months earlier, during the Chappelle row:

> *"Lenny Bruce was arrested...not by 'the public', but by the state. Dave
> Chappelle is facing criticism which is, I'm told, different."*

That is the whole argument in two sentences, and it is aimed precisely at the
martyrdom analogy the position depends on. Set against **16 January 2019** —
*"The recent joke shaming of Louis CK is so fucking disturbing"* — the move
happens somewhere in the thirty-three months between, and the earliest dated
instance of the new position is **2021-10-26**, not March 2022.

The O&A page's 2022 example is not wrong; it is just not first. Corrected
there rather than left for the next reader to trip over.

## January 6th: a conspiracy entertained, priced, and one rejected

The Capitol riot produces the year's densest cluster, and it is the best
available demonstration of what
`wiki/mind/synthesis/vertical-authority-skepticism` means when it says the
"conspiracy crank" label is contradicted by his behaviour.

**He forms one.** On 7 January: *"i'm as sure as i could possibly be that the
capitol police had arranged to allow the chuds into the building while they
LARPed the violence they would usually be committing"* — a serious accusation
of collusion by a police force, stated at high confidence.

**Then he immediately prices it, in the same tweet:** *"but what was the
endgame? is that being too generous"*. The hypothesis is published with its own
weakest point attached, and the weakest point is that it credits the actors
with more coherence than the evidence supports.

**And he rejects the mirror-image conspiracy on structural grounds.** On
17 January, to somebody arguing antifa infiltration: *"Sooooooo...are you saying
that the radical leftists were agitating to keep the far-right president in
power rather than the democratic candidate? Do you seriously think that antifa
is working against their own ideological values to sling mud on Trump
supporters?"* The refutation is not "that's a conspiracy theory" — it is that
the theory requires its actors to work against their own interests.

That is the distinction the whole vertical-authority page rests on: he is not
credulous about institutions and he is not credulous about the stories told
against them either. The test he applies is whether the actors' behaviour makes
sense from inside their own position, and he applies it to his own hypothesis
first.

## Texture

*"gonna exec produce a new primetime series that is just conservatives in a
restraining chair (like the theater scene from a clockwork orange) and make
them define terms they constantly use incorrectly such as: socialism,
globalism, obamagate, liberty/freedom"* (5 January) — the definitional-precision
instinct as a revenge fantasy. Matt Gaetz *"is a lot more tolerable if you just
pretend he is actually a 4th grader who switched bodies with an Arizona State
undergrad"* (15 January). And on 12 November, a small perfect one: he
misreads a tweet in somebody's likes, believes for twelve hours that his old
coach is coaching in the NFL, **telephones his mother about it**, and then
posts the correction himself.

## What would change this reading

The Chappelle correction is solid — it is a dated post making the argument, and
the O&A page's own example is later. The Jan 6 reading interprets a
self-qualification as method rather than as hedging, which is a real
alternative; the reason to prefer method is the 17 January rejection, which
applies the same test to the opposite conspiracy at cost to his own side's
narrative. And 34 posts is a small year to characterise a position from — the
vocabulary is unambiguous, but the absence of any internal *doubt* about the
position may be an artefact of how little he posted.
